messages.content:
The `printHelp` method in the `HelpFormatter` class handles printing help information, including the command line syntax, header, options, and footer. The `Option` class constructor initializes an option with an option name and a description.

Looking at the failing test `testInfiniteLoop`, it sets a very small width of 20 for the formatter and then tries to print help for an option with a long description. This triggers an infinite loop in the wrapping code of `HelpFormatter`, causing the JVM to crash with an OutOfMemoryError.

The current bug report confirms this behavior by describing how the `HelpFormatter` goes into an infinite loop when there isn't enough space to display a word on a single line.

To fix this issue, the width of the formatter should be set to a value that can accommodate the length of the description to prevent the infinite loop from occurring.

Next, I will provide the methods that need to be fixed:

1. `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printHelp(java.io.PrintWriter, int, java.lang.String, java.lang.String, org.apache.commons.cli.Options, int, int, java.lang.String, boolean)`
2. `org.apache.commons.cli.Option.Option(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

```

org.apache.commons.cli.Option.Option(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)
```
